A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamBench++ and retain identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, tables, and figures. Their main texts and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven image generators, human ratings, evaluator-alignment measurements, prompt ablations, and reproduction experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons across additional multimodal evaluators in Section 4.4 and Table 7.

M1.justification: The proposed evaluation procedure retains numerical 0–4 ratings, task-specific instructions, internal thinking, and summary/planning. Testing additional evaluator models does not establish a change to this procedure or its default GPT-4o evaluator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DreamBench and the same DreamBench++ coverage of 150 reference images and 1,350 prompts, including the same subject and prompt categories. CustomConcept101 is newly discussed but not experimentally evaluated; Appendix C's single-image discussion adds no new test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 7 substantially broadens evaluator comparisons by adding GPT-4o-2024-08-06, GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18, Claude-3.5-Sonnet-20241022, and Gemini-1.5-Pro-001 against the original GPT-4o evaluator. The seven image generators, DINO/CLIP comparisons, and existing GPT-4V ablation remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 4 replace Krippendorff's alpha with Pearson correlation for the central human-alignment comparison, while Table 3 retains alpha. Table 2 also adds CP/PF as a diagnostic metric. These change the evaluation framework; the documented data, annotation requirements, and generator training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a targeted transfer analysis across evaluator families and GPT-4o versions, extending the earlier evaluator-capability investigation. The prompt-component, GPT-4V, CoT, and in-context-learning ablations are retained without changed results.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 adds ± uncertainty reporting for DINO–human and CLIP–human correlations, whereas v1 reported ± values only for GPT–human alignment there. Neither version explains the uncertainty estimator or supplies repeated-run counts, so this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces central alignment results: its GPT–human ratios change from 79.64%/93.18% under alpha to 83.31%/98.17% as printed under Pearson; v2 Section 4.1 instead states 98.71%. These are different-metric results, not same-setting gains. Table 7 adds evaluator results spanning 63.04%–84.23%, and Table 2 adds CP/PF values. The original generator scores and reproduction results are retained.

T1.justification: Table 2 introduces the derived quantity CP/PF as a diagnostic alongside the existing CP·PF ranking score. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition; neither version develops corresponding proofs or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The central claims of an automated, human-aligned, diverse benchmark remain. The introduction revises the claimed advantages over traditional metrics from +54.1%/+50.7% to +32.59%/+37.23%, adds an explicit diversity contrast with CustomConcept101, and softens DreamBooth's 'best overall' characterization.

C2.justification: v1 attributes TI/DreamBooth score drops partly to reduced training and possible non-convergence; v2 instead attributes them to complex or stylized inputs. New Appendix C argues for single-image sufficiency and adds explanations and recommendations involving SDXL, feature injection, identity preservation, and prompt adherence. Section 3.2 also newly interprets CP/PF as an overfitting diagnostic.

D1.justification: Table 7 newly identifies the original evaluator as GPT-4o-2024-05-13 and supplies specific identifiers for the additional evaluators. The implementation appendix retains the same training hyperparameters, inference settings, negative prompts, and adapter scale. The project link's destination is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited research coverage, including personalization works such as PALP, UniPortrait, and OmniGen, plus additional multimodal and audio research in future directions. The introduction and Section 2.2 newly position DreamBench++ against CustomConcept101's stated diversity limitations, extending the existing DreamBench/VIEScore positioning.

P1.justification: Prose is condensed and edited across the introduction, dataset construction, and experimental discussion. The qualitative analysis moves to Appendix A, the ablation subsection becomes a paragraph within main results, and appendices are reorganized. Author affiliations, publication headers, and citation style change, while the main narrative sequence remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7 and a CP/PF column to Table 2, adopts conference formatting, and revises captions and table headers. The qualitative collage moves from v1 Figure 7 to v2 Figure 9 in Appendix A. Existing failure-case images are retained, although their caption now attributes results to Emu2, DreamBooth, and TI.

improvement.justification: The new cross-MLLM comparison strengthens evidence for evaluator portability, and Appendix C adds practical discussion. However, v2 combines retained introductory alpha percentages with Pearson-based margins, and Section 4.1's 98.71% conflicts with Table 4's 98.17%. It also drops v1's training-convergence caveat without adding a controlled experiment separating training effects from task difficulty. Stronger validation and weaker reporting coherence coexist, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
